articles.headline: Spurs-Pelicans games in Paris, Manchester sold out, NBA says
articles.description: The NBA announced on Tuesday that tickets are sold out for the 2027 NBA Paris and Manchester games set for January, featuring the San Antonio Spurs and the New Orleans Pelicans.
articles.body:
The NBA announced on Tuesday that tickets are sold out for the 2027 NBA Paris and Manchester games set for January, featuring the San Antonio Spurs and the New Orleans Pelicans.

According to the league, approximately one million fans registered interest in tickets, marking the highest level of demand recorded for NBA Games in Europe.

The Spurs and Pelicans will play regular season games at Accor Arena in Paris, France on Jan. 14, then face off again three days later at the Co-op Live in Manchester, England as part of the NBA's multiyear agreement to play regular-season outings in Europe.

Basketball ranks as the fastest-growing sport in Europe, according to the NBA, just behind soccer with more than 270 million fans across the continent. In fact, a record-71 Europeans made opening-night rosters last season in the NBA, and represent approximately 15% of the league, not to mention five of the last eight players to win MVP.

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Loss of Dart filters down to rest of Giants' skill position players
articles.description: Jaxson Dart's injury has a cascading effect on the Giants, whose skill players also take a hit.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 22: Giants take a hit with loss of Jaxson Dart, uncertainty around Bears starting QB

By Michael F. Florio

Adam Schefter reported on Tuesday that tests revealed that Jaxson Dart's knee injury is worse than initially thought, and the QB is now facing the possibility of season-ending surgery. Dart missing the season would be a crushing blow for the fantasy stock of Giants players.

Jameis Winston is the next man up. While that's meant good things for his receivers in the past, he looked rough on Monday night. Given his past tendencies to lock in and pepper his top receiver with targets, Malik Nabers still has fantasy hope. While this news drops Nabers into more of the WR2 range for the rest of the season, he still does bring upside given his immense talent ... just expect more weekly volatility as well. If Nabers' managers are panicking after his 1.1 fantasy points on Monday with Winston under center, it could be a good time to buy low.

Isaiah Likely remains a TE1, though his fantasy ceiling does take a hit here (Likely was targeted nine times by Winston, making for a 33% target share). While this news could mean the Giants become a more run-heavy offense, that would help keep Cam Skattebo afloat. His fantasy value still takes a slight hit as there will be less consistent scoring chances without Dart, but he should see enough volume to remain in the low-end RB2 range.

Some QBs managers can look to add to replace Dart in one-QB leagues are Kyler Murray, Tyler Shough, Bryce Young and C.J. Stroud. As for Winston, he is purely an option for superflex leagues and is more of a depth-piece QB3 than a starter.

Bears' starting QB up in the air for Week 3

Tyson Bagent is in the concussion protocol and his status is up in the air for Week 3. With Caleb Williams dealing with a hamstring injury, that would leave veteran Case Keenum as the starter for the Chicago Bears. To make matters trickier, the Bears play on "Monday Night Football", so fantasy managers will have to decide what to do with their Bears players on Sunday, potentially without knowing who will be starting at QB.

For those looking to replace Williams, the options to replace Dart (Murray, Shough, Young and Stroud) are good options here, too. For those in superflex, your options are more limited, as you can add Marcus Mariota or Winston.

articles.headline: Macdonald says Broncos' Payton accused Seahawks of cheating
articles.description: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald says the Broncos wrongfully accused Seattle of a Spygate-like cheating scandal in 2024. Denver coach Sean Payton ultimately "backed off" after the Seahawks threatened a lawsuit if they went public with the allegation.
articles.body:
Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald says the Denver Broncos wrongfully accused Seattle of a Spygate-like cheating scandal in 2024.

Broncos coach Sean Payton ultimately backed off after the Seahawks threatened a lawsuit if Denver went public with the allegation, according to Macdonald.

The saga came to light in a clip that surfaced Tuesday from Macdonald's recently published appearance on "In Depth With Graham Bensinger."

The Seahawks and Broncos opened the 2024 season at Lumen Field in Macdonald's first game as Seattle's coach. Seattle won 26-20, holding Denver to 231 total yards in quarterback Bo Nix's NFL debut.

"Fans will post plays from training camp on Twitter, so it's like public knowledge," Macdonald told Bensinger. "We took like 100 plays from their training camp. We were scouting them."

Payton later learned that the Seahawks had seen some of Denver's plays, called Seahawks general manager John Schneider and "lost it," according to Macdonald.

"He got wind of it and he lost it," Macdonald said of Payton. "This is the middle of the season, and we won the game. We were in the fight our first year. There was a lot of s--- going on. So he called John. He basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot Spygate type of thing.

"I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my god. We didn't cheat.' They thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant and the whole thing. So we had to counter with him and say, 'If you come out with this, we're going to sue you because it's not true.'"

Macdonald said Payton ultimately "backed down."

"The season ends and he let it go," Macdonald said. "But it was like the Cold War. He's like, 'I'm going to hit the button. I'm going to hit the button.' 'Well, we're going to hit the button.' None of us hit the button."

Macdonald said he and Payton ran into each other at the combine after the season, and nothing came of it.

Under Macdonald, the Seahawks have been among the teams that do not allow fans to film plays during training camp practices.

The Seahawks play the Broncos in Denver in Week 6.

articles.headline: Red Sox commit to Chad Tracy, Craig Breslow through 2030
articles.description: The Red Sox signed Chad Tracy to a three-year contract as manager while also exercising the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox, who are heading to the postseason following a remarkable run over the second half of the season, rewarded the two chief architects of that turnaround Tuesday.

Boston removed the interim tag and named Chad Tracy the 49th manager in team history, signing him to a three-year contract that will run through the 2029 season, with a club option for 2030. The Red Sox also announced that they have exercised the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.

The elevation of 41-year-old Tracy comes after the Red Sox secured a wild-card spot in the playoffs Sunday. Tracy took over in April after former manager Alex Cora was fired following a 10-17 start to the season.

"I think there was pretty much an understanding when I first got here that we've a lot of work to do, let's focus on that. Let's worry about the rest of the stuff later as it goes along," Tracy said during Tuedsay's news conference at Fenway Park.

"I am very happy, though, that it is done and in the course of three days we've clinched a playoff spot and now all the focus can be on what we can try to do in October."

Tracy has since guided the Red Sox to a 74-55 record, which included a 15-game win streak that tied the franchise record set in 1946. Boston's 27-3 (.900) record from July 3 through Aug. 7 was the best 30-game span in franchise history.

It's a remarkable turnaround for a team that was 32-46 and 15½ games back in the American League East race on June 24.

"Chad came into an incredibly difficult situation in April and provided stability and leadership when this organization needed it most," Red Sox president Sam Kennedy said. "We had conversations with Craig over the summer and got that extension done."

Breslow said he announced Tracy's new deal during a team meeting in the clubhouse about 15 minutes before the news conference.

"That was cool. I choked up a little bit," Tracy said, smiling.

Breslow, 46, was hired in October 2023. A 2013 World Series champion with Boston, he is only the fourth former Red Sox player to lead the club's baseball operations efforts.

In his three seasons in the role, the Red Sox have gone 254-226 (.529), the third-best record in the AL.

Tracy had served as the manager of the Red Sox's Triple-A team in Worcester since 2022, leading the WooSox to a winning record in each of his four full seasons as manager. That came after seven previous years managing in the Los Angeles Angels' minor league system.

He's the son of former big-league manager Jim Tracy, who managed the Dodgers (2001-05), Pirates (2006-07) and Rockies (2009-12).

"I was along for the ride on my dad's journey," Chad Tracy said. "I stayed up late to talk to him to learn the game. I was fascinated by it. I really was."

Jim Tracy was named interim manager of the Rockies in May 2009, led them to a 74-42 turnaround and won NL manager of the year. It's a similar run to his son's.

articles.headline: Yankees don't expect Aaron Judge (calf) back for wild card
articles.description: Aaron Judge is not expected to be available for the Yankees' wild-card series as he continues to recover from a calf strain.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Yankees manager Aaron Boone said he does not expect to have Aaron Judge available for the Wild Card series next week, though he did not completely rule out the star right fielder recovering from his calf strain in time to play.

"We're planning on him not being a part of that," Boone said Tuesday before the Yankees hosted the Tampa Bay Rays for a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.

Judge was placed on the injured list with a right calf strain Friday, two days after exiting a game against the Minnesota Twins with the injury. Judge and the team declined to specify the severity of the injury through the weekend. On Tuesday, Boone labeled it a "moderate grade" strain. He said Judge received a PPP injection Monday and will avoid physical activity over the "next couple days."

"You hear all the time with injuries, we get ranges," Boone said. "Two to four weeks, four to six, all these things. There are ranges for a reason, and we're at a point in the year where obviously we push it a little bit if that was in play. But that's a week away so I'm not expecting it, but I'm not ruling it out either."

Judge, 34, sustained the injury in his seventh game back after missing more than three months with a fractured rib. The three-time MVP returned without going on a rehab assignment and went 4-for-23 with 13 strikeouts, one walk, and one home run in 24 plate appearances. He will likely finish his injury-plagued campaign with a .241 batting average, 18 home runs and an .871 OPS in just 66 games after two historic MVP seasons.

The Yankees are 41-25 in games Judge plays this season. They're 49-41 in games he doesn't play after a 2-0 win in the first game of Tuesday's doubleheader behind eight scoreless innings from Carlos Rodón.

"We have a lot of talent in this locker room and we have a lot of depth," said Yankees left fielder Cody Bellinger, who delivered a two-run home run in Tuesday's win. "I think a lot of different guys have stepped up, whether it's their first year in the big leagues or getting traded or whoever. We've had a lot of guys come in, step up, and continue playing winning baseball."

Heliot Ramos started in right field for the fourth straight game since Judge's absence in Tuesday's opener. Spencer Jones is another option to play right field in the postseason should Trent Grisham, who is on the injured list with a hamstring injury, return to play center field.

The Rays entered Tuesday's doubleheader with a magic number of one to clinch the American League East title with seven games remaining. Barring a Rays collapse, the Yankees will host the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card series for the second consecutive year.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA free agency: Grades for offseason signings, extensions
articles.description: We're grading the biggest free agent signings and extensions, including Kawhi Leonards's extension with the Raptors.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Sept. 22: Leonard, Raptors agree to $115 million extension

Kawhi Leonard terms: Two years, $115 million, with player option in second year

Grade: B-

An extension agreement between Leonard and the Raptors seemed like a fait accompli as early as June, when the Raptors and Clippers first agreed on the terms of Leonard's eventual trade to Toronto. Leonard was set to enter the final season of his controversial contract, and the Raptors wouldn't have wanted to trade multiple unprotected picks for a one-year rental.

This new deal will pay Leonard about $11 million less than his possible maximum, per ESPN's Shams Charania, which is capped at two years because of the NBA's over-38 rule. Leonard, now 35, will turn 38 years old at the end of this extension.

Just because an extension was expected, however, doesn't mean it's an incredible value for the team involved. Leonard now projects to have among the dozen highest cap hits in the league during this deal. And while he's also one of the dozen best players in the NBA if he's on the court -- and you can read about how optimistic I am about his fit in Toronto this upcoming season in my trade grade -- that's a major if for a player with his age and extensive injury history.

For comparison, last summer, Kevin Durant signed a new two-year contract with the Rockets, but that $90 million pact came with considerably greater savings for Houston. Leonard's new contract does give Toronto some extra wiggle room compared to if he had taken the max, but not by nearly the same amount.

Instead, Leonard's new deal seems more akin to the four-year, $273 million extension Donovan Mitchell signed this summer. Both deals were anticipated, given the stature the two stars hold in their respective franchises, but neither deal seems likely to age especially well. The Raptors and Cavaliers are both hoping that they win now, because these big new contracts could hamper their ability to win in the future.

Ausar Thompson terms: Five years, $155 million
